recipes.name: Best Beer Can Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 (12 fluid ounce) cans beer, half full

steps.text: Soak wood chips in water for at least 1 hour.
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect medium heat, about 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine sugar, salt, paprika, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl. Place beer cans on a baking sheet. Spoon 1 teaspoon seasoning mix into each can. Be careful, this will make beer foam up and out of the can.
Rub each chicken with 2 tablespoons oil. Rub remaining seasoning mix over entire chickens, inside and out. Place each chicken upright over 1 beer can.
Drain wood chips; place with coals, in an aluminum pan, or under the grill grate according to manufacturer’s instructions.

Place cans with chicken directly on the grill. Close the lid and grill chicken until no longer pink, and juices run clear, about 1 ½ hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of thighs should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Remove chickens from the grill; discard the beer cans. Cover chickens with a doubled sheet of aluminum foil; rest in a warm area before slicing, 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Beer Can Chicken
raw_recipe.description: In this best beer can chicken recipe, chicken is seasoned with a sweet and spicy brown sugar-paprika rub and grilled over wood chips for smoky flavor.

review.reviewBody: There's nothing quite like Beer Can Chicken at an outdoor BBQ! Ever since stumbling onto recipes like these here on AR we make these every summer. And, since there's never a shortage of beer in this house or neighbor's to help us eat these birds they've become a favorite. One I made with regular paprika and one I made with smoked paprika and I added a couple teaspoons of garlic powder to each one. It's much easier to take the seasoning mixture and blend it with melted butter vs. veg. oil and place half of it into the beer can and baste the chicken with the other half. Invest in the holder that you can purchase at Wal-Mart or Bed, Bath, & Beyond, you'll be glad you did!

Love this recipe, exactly as is is good, but I had a problem with the grill flaring up when the fat from the bird melted into the flames, and drying out the white meat too much. I then added a small cookie sheet between the chicken/beer can, and the grill grates. That really helped stabilize the temperature over the cooking time, and lead to a much more tender bird. Will use this recipe again with cookie sheet. Excellent recipe and spice mixture. Edit: six years later and I'm making these using an actual smoker. I keep everything the same except I also carefully separate the skin from the meat and add spice rub under the skin too. So far I've been cooking at the temperature noted. Next time I'll try to cook low and slow.

Very good. Did not use wood chips. Used less salt and cut ingredients in half as only doing one 6 lb chicken. Added garlic powder and celery salt 1 to 2 tsp of each. Turned chicken around every 20 to 30 minutes to cook more evenly

This beer can chicken was my first on a masterbuilt electric. I smoked it for 4 hours at 215 degrees. I used a tall boy suggested from the reviews. This was the best I've ever had. The juices poured out,fantastic thanks!

It was awesome, and my daughter loved it! I had to make some adjustments but it turned out fine! 

I added about a quarter cup of Maple Syrup for a Canadian twist. I also added a splash of beer as the rub was a little thick. It was very windy (and cold. Ahh, Canadian spring!) to keep BBQ at right temp, so I brought it indoors and used Convection setting on oven.

Will definitely be a keeper around here!
Used 25% of the salt and increased all other ingredients proportionally. Fantastic. The most tender and juicy chicken you could ask for. Great recipe. Definitely will use it again.

I used this recipe as my template - I sprayed the chicken with cooking spray, rubbed on my favorite spices and used the rest for the beer can. Wood chips are a must! I used indirect heat (one side of grill turned off), kept the temp at 350 turning the chicken around halfway thru. Best chicken ever - moist and tender and flavorful. We are SO using this to make dinner for Father's Day. Best thing? No hot oven to overheat the house during the summer. Thanks, this is a keeper! :)
I greatly reduced the amount of added salt and cut the amount of sugar by a third. The result was very tasty and I will make it again.

It was amazing and tender. We put it in our smoker at about 275-300 degrees and cooked it for about 2 hours and it was falling a part tender. I added a bit of bbq rub to the chicken and the beer. 
Best chicken ever BBQ'd/smoked.

I also put a small red potato over the neck of the chicken so the meat steams from the inside and stays nice and moist. you could also use small balls of aluminum foil. 6/24/2010 For those of you that don't have a rack use a 24oz can for more leverage. 7/11/2010 Sorry that's a 16oz can.
I used Redd's Apple Ale and it was superb!
first time making this, and it was incredible after 2 1/2 hrs on the smoker. moist, fall off the bone, will be making it again!

Don't worry if the skin burns, the meat will still be VERY moist and tender! I love this recipe and make it fairly often. Everyone raves how good it is. You can get the beer can holders at Lowe's or similar home store.
I would make it again. I added Tbsp onion powder, Tbsp garlic, and added Tbsp cayenne and used Apple beer
Wow... I have made beer can chicken in the past but this one was very tasty and moist. Everyone kept talking about how delicious it was.
I omitted the wood chips and just made it on the grill. Also I used a local raspberry craft beer. My kids are asking for it again!
It was way to salty for me. Do like the overall taste but would use a lot less salt..
I have made this 10 times and it tastes better every time!
This is, for the most part, a great recipe. It's too salty, however, and I'll only use half the amount of salt next time.

Great combination of flavours in this rub. I prefer to add enough olive oil to the spices to make a 'sticking rub' and slather on clean, dried chicken. Leftover spices go into the can and a 1/2 lime placed into the top of the chicken for cooking. Thanks for sharing!
